findings.claim: Exactly one locally visible merge base is not sufficient evidence that the selected diff covers the inputs being executed. Two manifestations remain in the N2-05/N2-07 cause class: (a) a real depth-2 fetch hides one of two merge bases, returns rc=0/one SHA and an empty doc_diff, so the r3 predicate skips; (b) even with full history and one genuine merge base, a clean rename/modify merge transfers a PR edit from an unmonitored old path into a monitored fixture, while doc_diff(base, PR head) lists only the old path. The current CI checkout and event variables use different identities: merge checkout versus PR head. The r3 acceptance fixtures do not close these paths.

evidence.observed: Same-command controls: full two-base history selects full; depth-1/no-base selects full; missing head selects full; reverse push selects full; pushing the actual merge selects full; linear unrelated change still skips.

suggested_fix.where: K5 qualification in sections 2a-2c and acceptance 3/5, implemented in ci_dang_ky_test.py outside frozen doc_diff. This is the point that authorizes omission of mutation execution.
suggested_fix.how: Require complete history before using merge-base cardinality as evidence, otherwise run full. Bind the skip decision to the actual executed tree as well as the event head: validate the applicable push/head or PR/merge relationship, then include changed monitored inputs between the event base and that executed tree. Resolve both relevant contract directories safely; unresolved identity/history/directory information must select full. Comparing the scoped input blobs is another valid way to establish unchanged inputs. Preserve the existing unrelated-change skip control.
suggested_fix.locking_test_and_mutant: Run the original two parent-order criss-cross graphs, real depth-2 hidden-base clone, full-history rename/modify PR merge, missing-object/depth-1 cases, ordinary push and unrelated linear control in ONE command. Require --dot-bien for ambiguous history or changed executed inputs and no --dot-bien for the unrelated control. Kill one mutant omitting shallow-history qualification and one using only PR-head paths instead of executed-tree inputs; anchor each kill to its named target case.
suggested_fix.possible_new_failures: A blanket fallback can accidentally eliminate all PR savings; a comparison against the wrong tree can treat target-branch drift as a PR change or miss integration edits. Keep the negative control and explicit checkout identity tests. Do not execute historical Python to discover THU_MUC_HOP_DONG.

findings.limits: The current gate-registry pins fetch-depth: 0, so the shallow manifestation was demonstrated in a real scratch clone, not in a current CI run. The full-history merge manifestation does not require shallow history. These are executable selector-contract counterexamples, not execution of an absent r3 implementation, and do not establish that the complete registry would stay green forever.
